brief: Add a check that tells a billing specialist whether a denied claim can still be appealed. An appeal is allowed up to 120 days after the denial date, counting the denial date as day 0. After day 120 it is not allowed. Return how many days are left, or 0 when the window has closed.
facts: Made-up examples: denied on 2026-01-10, checked on 2026-03-10 gives 61 days left. Checked on 2026-05-10 (day 120) gives 0 days left but still allowed. Checked on 2026-05-11 is closed. All data is made up.

brief: Flag duplicate claims in a batch so a specialist can review them. Two claims are duplicates when they look the same.
facts: A claim has claimId, patientRef (a made-up code), serviceDate, procedureCode and amount. All data is made up.

brief: Calculate a student's final grade from weighted category scores. Homework counts 20%, quizzes 30%, the exam 50%. In the homework category the lowest score is dropped when there are 4 or more scores. Round the final grade to 1 decimal place.
facts: Made-up example: homework 90, 80, 70, 100 (drop 70, average 90), quizzes 80 and 70 (average 75), exam 60. Final = 0.2*90 + 0.3*75 + 0.5*60 = 70.5. A category with no scores counts as 0.

brief: Tell a counsellor when a student has missed 3 school days in a row. Weekends and school holidays do not count as school days and do not break a streak. Return the date the streak reached 3, or nothing.
facts: Input is a list of school days in date order, each marked present or absent, with holidays already removed. Made-up example: absent on Thursday, Friday and the next Monday is a streak of 3 reached on Monday.

brief: Price a promotion where a 10% discount and a buy-3-get-1-free offer can both apply to the same product line. Return the line total.
facts: A line has sku, units and unitPrice. Made-up example: 8 units at 5.00 normal price is 40.00.

brief: Work out when a distributor should reorder a product. The reorder point is the average daily sales times the supplier lead time in days, plus a safety stock of 20% of that lead-time demand. Recommend a reorder when stock on hand is at or below the reorder point.
facts: Made-up example: sells 50 a day, lead time 6 days: lead-time demand 300, safety stock 60, reorder point 360. Stock 360 recommends a reorder; stock 361 does not.

brief: Calculate simple interest owed on a loan for a date range. Interest is the principal times the annual rate times the number of days divided by 365. The start date counts, the end date does not. In a leap year the divisor is still 365. Round to 2 decimals.

Raise an alert when an account makes more than 5 card payments within any 10 minute period. Return the time of the payment that caused the alert. Payments exactly 10 minutes apart are in different periods.
facts: Input is a list of payment times in order, in UTC. Made-up example: payments at 10:00, 10:02, 10:04, 10:06, 10:08, 10:09 alert at 10:09. Payments at 10:00 and 10:10 are not in the same period.

brief: Check whether two delivery time windows on the same day overlap, so dispatch can avoid double booking a driver. Windows that only touch at an end (one ends at 12:00, the next starts at 12:00) do not overlap. Return the length of the overlap in minutes.
facts: A window has start and end as HH:mm. Made-up example: 09:00 to 11:00 and 10:30 to 12:00 overlap by 30 minutes. 09:00 to 12:00 and 12:00 to 13:00 overlap by 0.
